title: Sample Preparation and Optical Tweezers Study of Nanodisc-Embedded ABC Transporter OpuA
author: van der Sleen, van den Noort, et al.
materials: Here, we describe the preparation of crude membrane vesicles from cells that expressed our protein of interest. The protocol is based on van den Noort et al.7 We first disrupt the cells, then remove the soluble fraction, and wash and collect the crude membrane vesicles.CRITICAL: 20% (v/v) glycerol is been added in each step to prevent dissociation of the OpuAA subunits from the OpuA complex. See7 for a more elaborate overview on the conditions to prevent loss of the OpuAA subunits. All steps are performed on ice or in a cooled environment (4°C – 8 °C) to ensure stability of the protein, unless otherwise indicated.6.Cells and buffer preparation:a.If the cells have been stored at −80 °C, thaw them in a beaker of lukewarm water (∼ 40 °C).i.Stir or shake the cells gently every minute to make sure that the cells on the periphery will not get too warm while the cells on the inside are still frozen.Note: Thawing takes approximately 15 min.ii.Place the cells on ice once they are thawed.b.Prepare 200 – 400 mL of 50 mM KPi, pH 7.5, 20% (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM DTT (buffer A).Note: DTT should be freshly added.7.Cell disruption:a.Add 100 μg/mL DNase, 1 mM DTT and 2 mM MgSO4 to the cell suspension.b.Slowly add 1 mM PMSF (prepared as a 100 mM stock in isopropanol), while stirring to make sure the PMSF is distributed evenly.c.Rupture the cells by passing them twice through a cooled high-pressure homogenizer HPL6 (Maximator GmbH; 30 kPsi) or an equivalent device.Note: Make sure that the Maximator has been washed with buffer A prior to the addition of the cells. Additionally, it is possible to wash the Maximator with some buffer A after breaking the cells to increase the yield.d.Add 5 mM Na-EDTA, pH 8.0 to the lysed cells.e.Pellet the cell debris by low-speed centrifugation at 15,000 g (e.g., with a Beckman JA-25.50 rotor) for 20 min at 4 °C.f.Transfer the supernatant to ultracentrifugation tubes by pouring.Note: Make sure not to take any of the white pellet. Sometimes, a lot of the white pellet comes along when pouring out the supernatant. If this happens, the low-speed centrifugation (Step 7E) can be repeated with the supernatant. If the same is observed more frequently, more DNAse can be added in Step 7A.8.Isolation of the membrane fraction:a.Pellet the membrane fraction by ultracentrifugation at 185,000 g (e.g., with a Beckman 50.2-Ti rotor) for 75 min at 4 °C.Alternatives: The membrane fraction can also be collected by ultracentrifugation at 138,000 g (e.g., with a Beckman 45-Ti rotor) for 135 min at 4 °C.b.Remove the supernatant, containing the soluble protein fraction.c.Retrieve the pellet.i.Add a few mL of buffer A to the centrifugation tube and carefully mix with a pestle to release the pellet.ii.Transfer to a potter tube and repeat for all tubes.iii.Wash the centrifuge tube a few times with buffer A to retrieve all the material.d.Homogenize the membrane fraction.i.Add 25 – 50% of the original volume of buffer A.ii.Rotate and move the pestle up and down in the potter tube.iii.Repeat this until it forms a homogeneous and uniform suspension, and no particles of the membrane pellet are visible anymore.CRITICAL: Make sure to do this as gently as possible (i.e., try to prevent formation of air bubbles) as this may induce dissociation of OpuAA from the complex.e.Transfer the solution to ultracentrifugation tubes and repeat the ultracentrifugation step.f.Remove the supernatant, transfer the pellet to a potter tube and homogenize in buffer A. Use 10 mL buffer A per ∼100 mL cells of an OD600 of 200.9.Total protein concentration determination:a.Determine the total protein concentration with the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., Waltham, Massachusetts), using BSA as a standard (0 – 80 μg/mL).Note: Make sure to dilute the protein to an appropriate measurement range. The expected concentration is 8 – 16 mg/mL.b.Aliquot the crude membrane vesicles (CMVs) in samples of 18 mg.Pause Point: The CMVs can be flash frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C for several months when the protein is required for labeling. We have observed that the cysteines are less reactive to maleimides when the CMVs have been stored at −80 °C for more than a year. CMVs that are not used for labeling can be stored for a longer time.

We use a volume of 700 – 1000 μL in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube to minimize the dead-volume in the tube.Table 4Example of reconstitution mixtureReagentFinal concentrationAmountMQN/A361 μL1 M KPi, pH 7.050 mM KPi, pH 7.032 μL7.3 mM (5.63 mg/mL) lipids900 μM123 μL190 μM MSP1E3D145 μM237 μL1 M DTT1 mM1 μL18.3 μM (4 mg/mL) OpuA4.5 μM246 μLTotalN/A1,000 μLb.Nutate for 1 h at 4 °C.c.Add 500 mg semi-dry activated SM-2 BioBeads.d.Nutate overnight at 4 °C (∼ 16 h).Note: When weighing the BioBeads, make sure to remove most of the water before weighing.e.Remove the BioBeads the following day by transferring the solution with a pipette to a 2 mL Bio-Rad column and collecting the flow through.f.Remove the aggregates by centrifugation at 20,817 g for 15 min at 4 °C.CRITICAL: It is essential to immediately continue labeling the protein on the same day.

steps.title: Thaw cells and prepare buffer A
steps.instruction: If cells are stored at –80 °C, thaw them in ~40 °C water for ~15 min while gently stirring; then place on ice. Prepare 200–400 mL of buffer A (50 mM KPi, pH 7.5, 20 % v/v glycerol, 1 mM DTT, freshly added).

steps.title: Disrupt cells and low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Add to the cell suspension 100 µg/mL DNase, 1 mM DTT, 2 mM MgSO₄ and 1 mM PMSF (100 mM stock in isopropanol) while stirring. Lyse cells by passing twice through a cooled high‑pressure homogenizer (30 kPsi). Add 5 mM Na‑EDTA pH 8.0, then centrifuge at 15 000 g for 20 min at 4 °C. Transfer the supernatant to ultracentrifugation tubes, avoiding the white pellet.

steps.title: Isolate membrane fraction
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge the supernatant at 185 000 g for 75 min at 4 °C (alternative: 138 000 g for 135 min). Discard the supernatant, add a few mL of buffer A to the pellet, mix with a pestle, and transfer to a potter tube. Wash the pellet repeatedly with buffer A, then homogenize by adding 25–50 % of the original volume of buffer A and gently moving the pestle until no visible particles remain. Transfer back to ultracentrifuge tubes, repeat the ultracentrifugation, discard supernatant and homogenize the final pellet in buffer A (use 10 mL buffer A per ~100 mL cells at OD₆₀₀ = 200).

steps.title: Determine protein concentration and aliquot
steps.instruction: Measure total protein with the Pierce BCA assay (BSA standard 0–80 µg/mL); expected concentration 8–16 mg/mL. Aliquot crude membrane vesicles (CMVs) as 18 mg samples. Flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C (avoid >1 year storage before labeling).

steps.title: Prepare synthetic lipid stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 12.1 mg DOPE, 3.1 mg DOPC and 9.8 mg DOPG for a 25 mg/mL stock (10 × 250 µL aliquots). Dissolve each lipid in chloroform (0.484 mL DOPE, 0.123 mL DOPC, 0.394 mL DOPG) in a spherical glass flask. Evaporate chloroform at ~450 mbar, 40 °C while rotating (30 min–1 h). Close the valve, apply maximum vacuum and incubate 30 min to remove residual solvent.

steps.title: Form even lipid film with diethyl ether
steps.instruction: Add diethyl ether in the same total volume as the original chloroform (1 mL) to the dried lipids, rotate without vacuum to dissolve, then evaporate at ~850–900 mbar, 40 °C until dry (~5 min). Apply maximum vacuum for another 30 min, then flow nitrogen through the flask to ensure complete removal of ether.

steps.title: Hydrate, sonicate and store lipids
steps.instruction: Transfer the dried film to a 15 mL Falcon tube twice, each time adding 1.25 mL 50 mM KPi pH 7.0 (50 % of the original chloroform volume) and rotating to resuspend (clumps will remain). Sonicate the suspension in an ice‑water bath for 16 cycles (15 s on, 45 s off, amplitude 77 µm) to obtain small unilamellar vesicles (SUVs). Aliquot 250 µL into 1.5 mL tubes, pierce lids, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C or in liquid N₂ for up to 1 year. Fuse SUVs to large multilamellar vesicles (LMVs) by three freeze‑thaw cycles (liquid N₂ freeze, 20–30 min thaw at ~20 °C).

steps.title: Prepare DDM stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve n‑dodecyl‑β‑d‑maltoside (DDM) in Milli‑Q water to 10 % w/v. Aliquot 1 mL portions, store at –20 °C (max two freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: Dilute maleimide‑oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Dilute purchased maleimide‑oligos to 100 pmol/µL in 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5, 0.1 mM EDTA. Prepare 10 µL aliquots (1 nmol each) and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: PCR amplify dsDNA handles
steps.instruction: On ice, assemble the master mix per 50 µL reaction: 5 µL 5× Taq buffer (1× final), 2 µL 10 mM dNTPs (200 µM final), 3 µL each of forward and reverse primers (1 µM final, 100 µM stock), 0.5 µL template DNA (0.83 µg/µL, 500 µg/mL stock), 1.5 µL Taq polymerase (25 units/mL, 1 U/µL). Dispense into six 50 µL tubes (total 300 µL per handle). Run PCR: 95 °C 2 min; 30 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 55 °C 15 s, 72 °C 45 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C. Clean up all six reactions on one column of a PCR clean‑up kit, elute with 30–40 µL Milli‑Q water. Verify 544 bp band on agarose gel, measure concentration (~200 ng/µL) by Nanodrop. Mix biotin‑ and digoxigenin‑functionalized handles 1:1. Store at –20 °C (aliquots ≈200 ng).

steps.title: Set laser power for smOT
steps.instruction: Adjust the 10 W 1064 nm laser to ~20 % output (≈2 W total). With a 50 % trap split and 10 % laser power, expect ≈170 mW per trap; at ~20 % overall power this corresponds to ≈340 mW per trap in the sample plane.

steps.title: Prepare catalase stock (85 000 U/mL)
steps.instruction: Resuspend catalase crystals by gentle agitation, transfer 1 000 000 U (≈100 µL suspension) to a 1.5 mL tube. Wash four times: resuspend in 1 mL Milli‑Q, centrifuge 17 000 g 5 min, discard supernatant. Finally resuspend pellet in 1.25 mL 50 mM KPi pH 7.0; dissolve at 37 °C with gentle agitation (tens of minutes). Aliquot 15 µL and store at 4 °C (max 3 months).

steps.title: Prepare glucose oxidase stock (1300 U/mL)
steps.instruction: Weigh 5.26 mg glucose oxidase, dissolve in buffer containing 20 mM HEPES‑K pH 7.0, 50 mM KCl, 50 % v/v glycerol. Aliquot 15 µL and store at –20 °C (max 3 months).

steps.title: Prepare 33 % glucose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 330 mg glucose in 1 mL Milli‑Q water, aliquot 15 µL and store at –20 °C (stable ≥1 year).

steps.title: Make measurement buffer with oxygen scavenger
steps.instruction: In 530 µL total volume mix: 10.6 µL 85 000 U/mL catalase, 10.6 µL 1300 U/mL glucose oxidase, 10.6 µL 33 % glucose (gives 0.66 % w/v final), and 498.2 µL measurement buffer (e.g., 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7, 50 mM NaCl). Filter through a 0.2 µm filter (use a small 15 mm filter).

steps.title: Solubilize synthetic lipids with DDM
steps.instruction: Thaw 250 µL of the 25 mg/mL lipid stock at ~20 °C. Dilute to 1 mL with 50 mM KPi pH 7.0 in a 15 mL Falcon tube. Tip‑sonicate in an ice‑water bath for 8 cycles (15 s on, 45 s off, amplitude 77 µm). Transfer 900 µL to a glass vial and incubate at ~20 °C in the dark with 100 µL 10 % w/v DDM.

steps.title: Solubilize crude membrane vesicles
steps.instruction: Thaw CMVs, keep on ice. Dilute on ice in MLA‑80 tubes to 3 mg/mL in a final volume of 6 mL containing 50 mM KPi pH 7.0–7.5, 20 % v/v glycerol, 200 mM KCl, 1 mM DTT and 0.5 % w/v DDM (example: 18 mg/mL CMVs → 1 mL). Incubate on ice 30 min, mixing once after 15 min. Ultracentrifuge at 336 896 g for 20 min at 4 °C to pellet insoluble material.

steps.title: Ni²⁺‑Sepharose affinity purification
steps.instruction: Equilibrate 0.5 mL Ni²⁺‑Sepharose in a 10 mL disposable column. Wash with 12 column volumes (CV) Milli‑Q water, then equilibrate with 4 CV buffer B (50 mM KPi pH 7.0, 200 mM KCl, 20 % v/v glycerol, 1 mM DTT, 0.04 % w/v DDM, 10 mM imidazole). Add the solubilized supernatant supplemented with 10 mM imidazole, let resin settle 10–20 min, mix gently, let settle again 10–20 min (no agitation). Drain, wash twice with 10 CV buffer B + 50 mM imidazole. Elute sequentially with 0.6 CV then four ×0.4 CV buffer B + 200 mM imidazole pH 7.5; collect five fractions (protein expected in fractions 3–4 at 3–5 mg/mL).

steps.title: Reconstitute OpuA into nanodiscs
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube combine to a final volume of 700–1000 µL: 900 µM lipids, 4.5 µM OpuA tetramer (two OpuABC + two OpuAA), 45 µM MSP1E3D1, 1 mM DTT, and 50 mM KPi pH 7.0. Incubate 1 h at 4 °C. Add 500 mg semi‑dry SM‑2 BioBeads, then incubate overnight (~16 h) at 4 °C. Remove BioBeads by passing the mixture through a 2 mL Bio‑Rad column, collect flow‑through. Centrifuge at 20 817 g for 15 min at 4 °C to remove aggregates. Proceed immediately to labeling (same day).

steps.title: Prepare measurement buffer (deoxygenate)
steps.instruction: Filter 20 mL measurement buffer through a 0.2 µm filter, then sonicate for 10 min.

steps.title: Clean and prime microfluidic system
steps.instruction: With the system depressurized, remove the 70 % ethanol from syringes (only the liquid around the edge). Add 1 mL Milli‑Q to each syringe, run 500 µL through the chip at 1.8 bar to flush ethanol. Stop flow. Repeat with 1 mL measurement buffer. (Optional) Passivate by flowing 1 mg/mL BSA in Milli‑Q at 0.2 bar for 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin bead solution (channel 1)
steps.instruction: Vortex streptavidin‑coated beads 30–60 s. Dilute 1 µL of 1 % w/v bead stock into 500 µL measurement buffer, vortex the suspension.

steps.title: Prepare measurement buffer with scavenger (channel 2)
steps.instruction: Mix the components listed in the oxygen‑scavenger table (85 000 U/mL catalase, 1 700 U/mL, 1300 U/mL glucose oxidase, 26 U/mL, 0.66 % w/v glucose) to a total of 530 µL, filter through a 0.2 µm filter.

steps.title: Prepare protein‑AD bead solution (channel 3)
steps.instruction: Incubate labeled OpuA with 200 ng dsDNA handles (incubation time/temperature as determined previously; keep at 4–8 °C). Dilute the incubation 25‑fold (2 µL sample + 48 µL measurement buffer, giving ≈8 µg/mL protein). Vortex anti‑digoxigenin beads 30–60 s. Mix 20 µL diluted protein‑DNA with 10 µL anti‑dig beads, incubate 10 min at room temperature. Dilute the resulting mixture in 500 µL measurement buffer.

steps.title: Load solutions into microfluidic channels and measure
steps.instruction: Remove the previous buffer from syringes, load channel 1 streptavidin beads, channel 2 scavenger buffer, and channel 3 protein‑AD beads. Capture beads, calibrate traps, tether protein between beads, and perform smOT measurements.

steps.title: Clean microfluidic system after measurements
steps.instruction: With the system depressurized, remove all solutions from syringes. Add 1 mL Milli‑Q to each syringe and run 0.5 mL through the chip at 1.8 bar. Flush with 5 % v/v mucasol solution (run 0.5 mL at 1.8 bar, apply pressure waves to dislodge residual beads). Repeat flushing with Milli‑Q, then with 2 mL 70 % ethanol (run 0.5 mL at 1.8 bar).

steps.title: Optional: static chip preparation
steps.instruction: Assemble a static chip using two microscope slides, two small and two large parafilm strips; melt parafilm on an 80 °C hot plate, press a 18 × 18 mm cover‑slide onto the slide (parafilm becomes transparent). Rinse chamber with 120 µL MQ twice, then 120 µL 1 mg/mL BSA twice (incubate 5 min), flush with measurement buffer, then with oxygen‑scavenger buffer. Add 5 µL of each bead solution (as prepared for channels 1 and 3) to the respective chambers. Seal with vacuum grease and a strip of parafilm (or double‑sided tape).

steps.title: Analyze smOT data
steps.instruction: Load the .hdf5 file in analysis software (e.g., Igor Pro). Subtract the baseline force measured in the approach curve from all force‑distance traces. Fit the dsDNA handle stretching with an extensible worm‑like chain (contour length 370 nm, persistence length 20 nm, temperature 297 K, Hookean spring constant 400–1200 pN). Identify force‑distance rips and fit each with a standard WLC (persistence 0.7 nm) to obtain contour‑length changes. Assign each event to structural transitions using expected ΔL_c = #AAs × 0.365 nm – L_c,initial. For constant‑distance traces, first fit a corresponding constant‑velocity trace, then identify transitions via Hidden Markov Modeling, assign to events, and compute kinetic parameters: equilibrium probabilities, energy differences (ΔG = ‑k_BT ln P), and zero‑force rates by fitting rates versus force with an extended Zhurkov‑Bell‑Evans‑Richie model.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for sample preparation of the membrane protein OpuA reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs for measurements with single-molecule optical tweezers (smOT) (Figure 1A). However, the method is generally applicable for other proteins and membrane-mimicking constructs to measure (un)folding and conformational dynamics with smOT. Using this procedure for purification and reconstitution in lipid nanodiscs, a stable and homogenous sample can be obtained. The protocol additionally includes instructions on how to prepare double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) handles, how to label the protein for smOT measurements making use of cysteine-maleimide chemistry, and how to collect and analyze the smOT data.Figure 1Experimental setup and domain organization of OpuA(A) Schematic of the smOT setup where OpuA is tethered between two beads.(B) Gene organization of OpuA mutant K521C used for labeling.(C) Domain organization of OpuA, which is reconstituted into a lipid nanodisc. The structure of OpuA is based on PDB 7AHH, where the SBDs have been added manually. A and C have been reprinted and adapted from van der Sleen et al.1 published under the Creative Commons CC-BY license. For attaching dsDNA handles, we make use of a cysteine mutant of OpuA. OpuA is an oligomer, consisting of two OpuABC and two OpuAA proteins (Figures 1B and 1C).2,3 This means that we only have to introduce one cysteine mutation to create two attachment sites for dsDNA handles, which are used for pulling with smOT. The polypeptide OpuABC contains the substrate-binding domain (SBD), scaffold and the transmembrane domain (TMD). OpuAA consists of the nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) and cystathionine beta-synthase domain (CBS) (Figure 1C). The protein construct has a 6x-His-tag at the C-terminus of OpuABC (Figure 1B) which is used for purification. OpuA does not contain any native cysteines.
